question: In Internet technology, what does DNS stand for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Domain Name System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Domain Name System (DNS)** is a hierarchical and decentralized naming system used to identify computers, services, and other resources reachable through the Internet or other Internet Protocol (IP) networks.
 
• It translates more readily memorized domain names to the numerical IP addresses needed for locating and identifying computer services and devices with the underlying network protocols.
 
• DNS is an essential component of the functionality of the Internet, as it provides a worldwide, distributed directory service.
 
• It was introduced to provide an easier way to access websites without having to remember complex numeric IP addresses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **IP Address**

 
 
• An IP address is a unique string of characters that identifies each computer using the Internet Protocol to communicate over a network.
 
• IP addresses are used to locate and identify a device on the network.
 
• They come in two versions: IPv4 (e.g., 192.168.1.1) and IPv6 (e.g., 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334).
 
 
 
• **Top-Level Domain (TLD)**
 
 
• A Top-Level Domain (TLD) is the last segment of the domain name, the part that follows immediately after the "dot" symbol.
 
• Examples include .com, .org, .net, .edu, and country-specific TLDs like .in, .us, .uk.
 
 
 
• **DNS Server**
 
 
• A DNS server is a server that contains a database of public IP addresses and their associated hostnames, and in most cases, serves to resolve or translate those names to IP addresses as requested.
 
• There are different types of DNS servers: primary, secondary, authoritative, and caching servers.
 
 
 
• **DNS Resolver**
 
 
• A DNS resolver, also known as a DNS lookup, is the process by which a DNS client (usually a web browser) requests the IP address associated with a domain name.
 
• It is the starting point for any DNS query and is responsible for tracking down the requested information.
